events.title: Thirteenth Amendment Ratified
events.description: Georgia's ratification brought the Thirteenth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution to the three-fourths of states it needed. That made it part of the Constitution. The amendment abolished slavery and involuntary servitude, except as punishment for a crime.
events.significance: It formally ended legal slavery across the United States. It was the first of the Reconstruction-era amendments.

events.title: The Washington Post Publishes Its First Edition
events.description: The first issue of The Washington Post appeared in the U.S. capital. It began as a local newspaper.
events.significance: The paper grew into one of America's most influential news organizations. It is known for its political reporting.

events.title: Finland Declares Independence
events.description: Finland's parliament adopted a declaration of independence from Russia. This ended 109 years as a Grand Duchy within the Russian Empire. The move came amid the turmoil that followed the Russian Revolution.
events.significance: It created the modern Finnish state. Finland still marks December 6 as its Independence Day.

events.title: Anglo-Irish Treaty Signed
events.description: Irish and British delegates signed the Anglo-Irish Treaty in London. It ended the Irish War of Independence. It paved the way for the Irish Free State, a self-governing dominion within the British Empire.
events.significance: The treaty reshaped Ireland's political map. It also split Irish nationalists and led to the Irish Civil War.
